To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cryo-EM reconstructions of the pre-60S particle in different conformation states revealed how steric hindrances and molecular mimicry prevent both premature folding of the pre-ribosomal particle and binding of later ribosome assembly factors.

we determined the structure of the nucleolar 60 S ribosomal subunit precursor by cryo-electron microsopy at a resolution of 3.4 angstroms and that the structure reveals the mechanism by which ribosome assembly factors control and coordinate the folding of the large ribosomal subunit.

cryo-EM reconstructions of the early pre-60S particle reveal a ring-like structure of three Brix-domain factors that stabilize the architecture of the nucleolar 60 S precursor ribosomal subunit and that these structures rationalize previous data on ribosome biogenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying the assembly of the large ribosomal subunit (60S) in the nucleolus of eukaryotic cells.
the structure and function of the pre-60S subunit and its assembly factors.
the structure and function of pre-ribosomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is the first structure of a pre-60S subunit and that it is the most complete structure to date of any ribosome subunit.
the pre-60S particle is a highly dynamic structure, which is constantly changing its shape and conformation to achieve its final structure.

the structures reported here represent snapshots of the nucleolar 60 S pre-ribosomal subunit at different stages of maturation, and that the formation of this particle is a complex process involving multiple conformations and rearrangements of rRNA domains and ribosomal proteins, which is facilitated by the action of a large number of assembly factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pre-ribosomal particle is a complex molecular machine that is built up by the concerted action of multiple assembly factors.

we have solved the structure of a pre-60S subunit that is the most immature particle yet to be determined and that it is the first cryo-EM structure to show a pre-60 ribosome in an early stage of maturation.
the pre-60S particle is a dynamic assembly intermediate, which is stabilized by the concerted action of multiple assembly factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ribosome assembly is a highly dynamic process that is regulated by a large number of assembly factors that control the folding and remodeling of the rRNA and the incorporation of ribosomal proteins.
the pre-60S particle has to fold in a highly controlled manner to prevent premature folding of the polypeptides that are later translated.
the assembly factors act as a molecular toolbox to control and coordinate the formation of the large ribosomal subunit.
